canonicalCards.recommendedFirstExperiment: Automate a small gain change on one known harsh phrase, then compare with a dynamic treatment.
stopOrUndo: Stop once you can tell whether the targeted phrase improves without changing unaffected material. Undo or back off immediately if fast frequency/gain moves can cause tonal jumps or phase artifacts.
Return the parameter to its previous value or undo the automation edit.
canonicalCards.teachingPrinciple: Use automation when the tonal change follows known phrases or sections; use dynamic EQ when the response should follow signal level automatically.
canonicalCards.title: EQ parameter automation
tradeoffs: Fast frequency/gain moves can cause tonal jumps or phase artifacts.

contradictions.summary: Draw automation for precision / Perform automation for musical feel
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Use drawing for exact timing or discrete edits; perform when continuous gesture and phrasing matter, then edit either result.

contradictions.summary: Use Touch for local corrections that rejoin old data / Use Latch for new section states that should persist
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Choose by what should happen after release.

contradictions.summary: Use Write for complete rewrites / Avoid Write and use Touch/Latch for safety
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Write is appropriate only when replacing the entire traversed range is intentional.

contradictions.summary: Use track automation for mix timeline / Use region automation for reusable clip/phrase behavior
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Choose the owner that should carry the movement when regions move or copy.

contradictions.summary: Always move track automation with regions / Never move track automation with regions
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Use Ask while arranging; decide whether the move belongs to the region or song position.

contradictions.summary: Include automation trails with moved regions / Leave trails at the timeline position
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Include only when the post-region automation is truly part of that region's audible consequence.

contradictions.summary: Edit the absolute curve directly / Use relative automation for offsets
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Relative preserves the underlying contour; absolute is simpler when one final curve is desired.

contradictions.summary: Use Trim for a performed offset / Use Relative for a separate editable offset curve
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Trim is a mode of writing an offset; Relative stores a secondary curve.

contradictions.summary: Ride syllables first / Automate sections first
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Begin at the largest timescale that explains the problem, then refine.

contradictions.summary: Use compression for level consistency / Use manual rides for musical placement
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Compression reacts to level; rides follow musical judgment. Often combine them.

contradictions.summary: Ride before compression / Ride after compression
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Use pre for detector consistency; post for final placement.

contradictions.summary: Use region/clip gain / Use fader automation
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Pre-processing correction changes processor input; fader automation changes later placement.

contradictions.summary: Automate the source send / Automate the return fader
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Send changes what enters the effect; return changes the generated effect output.

contradictions.summary: Automate bypass / Automate Mix or send/return level
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Bypass may interrupt state/tails; Mix may preserve state but still process.

contradictions.summary: Use pre-fader sends for independent effects / Use post-fader sends so wet follows dry rides
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Choose according to whether wet/dry relationship should follow source level.

contradictions.summary: Automate one shared return / Automate individual source sends
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Return moves every source; sends provide source-specific control.

contradictions.summary: Increase reverb in choruses for size / Reduce reverb in dense choruses for clarity
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Section density and desired depth decide; size is not identical to wetness.

contradictions.summary: Automate a delay send / Duplicate/edit the word to a dedicated delay track
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Send automation is flexible; printed/dedicated events can be simpler and more deterministic.

contradictions.summary: Use continuous curves / Use stepped automation
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Continuous motion suits gradual changes; steps suit discrete states and rhythms.

contradictions.summary: Snap automation to the grid / Place automation by ear off-grid
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Use grid for rhythmically defined events; use ear-led timing for phrasing and transients.

contradictions.summary: Keep detailed controller data / Simplify to fewer points
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Keep only detail that changes the audible gesture.

contradictions.summary: Automate EQ at known moments / Use dynamic EQ to react automatically
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Known editorial timing favors automation; level-dependent behavior favors dynamic control.

contradictions.summary: Automate compressor threshold / Automate input/region gain
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Threshold changes detector criteria; input gain changes signal into the detector.

contradictions.summary: Switch a plug-in on/off / Crossfade parallel processed paths
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Switching is simple but can glitch; parallel crossfade preserves state but adds routing complexity.

contradictions.summary: Automate the group bus / Automate individual tracks
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Use bus for shared perspective; use members when internal balance must change.

contradictions.summary: Automate a VCA / Automate a summing aux
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: VCA changes member control offsets; aux changes summed audio and downstream processing.

contradictions.summary: Automate Master / Automate Stereo Output
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: In Logic they have different roles; use the actual output for final audio level unless global VCA offset is intended.

contradictions.summary: Use a hardware controller / Draw with mouse/trackpad
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Controller supports feel; mouse supports precise editing. Combine them.

contradictions.summary: Automate Smart Control macro / Automate underlying parameters
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Macro preserves perceptual intent; direct lanes expose exact processor behavior.

contradictions.summary: Expect each alternative to have its own track automation / Use shared track automation and alternative-specific region automation
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Logic shares track automation across alternatives.

contradictions.summary: Automate mute / Automate a short volume fade
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Mute is discrete; fade can avoid clicks and preserve desired transitions.

contradictions.summary: Automate from the beginning / Wait until static balance is stable
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Creative production can begin with automation; corrective mix automation benefits from a solid baseline.

contradictions.summary: Use mix-bus automation for section contrast / Avoid global parameter automation
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Small deliberate moves can work; global changes are high-impact and vulnerable to loudness bias.

contradictions.summary: Automate the weak section / Change arrangement or performance
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Automation presents material; arrangement changes the material itself.

contradictions.summary: Place points exactly on the grid / Offset automation to compensate timing
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Only offset after proving a consistent audible scheduling discrepancy.

contradictions.summary: Follow popular forum workflow / Follow current Logic documentation
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Use community patterns for practical hypotheses; official docs own current software behavior.

myths.myth: A good mix should not need automation

myths.correction: It can hide symptoms, but a poor baseline balance should usually be corrected first.
myths.myth: Automation can rescue a bad static balance

myths.correction: Write can erase existing automation across the traversed range even without a gesture.
myths.myth: Write mode is the easiest and safest mode

myths.correction: The fader is following stored automation as designed.
myths.myth: Read mode is broken when the fader snaps back

myths.correction: Off stops reading/writing; it does not delete the stored data.
myths.myth: Turning automation Off deletes it

myths.correction: Region automation, other parameters, MIDI CC, Smart Controls, or grouped control may remain.
myths.myth: Deleting the visible lane removes every automation path

myths.correction: Movement depends on automation type and the Move Track Automation with Regions setting.
myths.myth: Track automation always moves with regions

myths.correction: They differ in ownership, copying, movement, looping, and replacement behavior.
myths.myth: Region automation and track automation are interchangeable

myths.correction: It belongs to the region and may be lost when the region is replaced.
myths.myth: Region automation survives replacing or re-recording the region

myths.correction: Track-based automation is shared; region automation can differ per alternative.
myths.myth: Track Alternatives have separate track automation

myths.correction: Excess points can reproduce controller jitter and complicate editing.
myths.myth: More points make automation smoother

myths.correction: Fast or complex gestures may require detail; remove only redundant or inaudible points.
myths.myth: Fewer points are always better

myths.correction: Many parameter scales and source responses are nonlinear.
myths.myth: A straight visual ramp produces a perceptually even change

myths.correction: Phrase-led or transient-led automation may need off-grid placement.
myths.myth: Snapping every automation point improves timing

myths.correction: Plug-in latency, scheduling, smoothing, and trigger timing can shift audible response.
myths.myth: Automation exactly on the grid cannot sound late

myths.correction: It is a broad setting and should not be used before isolating the cause.
myths.myth: Automation Snap Offset is a per-track timing fix

myths.correction: Touch returns to prior data after release; Latch continues writing the held value.
myths.myth: Touch and Latch are basically the same

myths.correction: They are related offset concepts with different writing and storage behavior.
myths.myth: Trim and Relative are the same feature

myths.correction: Logic limits relative automation to supported parameters such as Volume, Pan, and Send levels.
myths.myth: Relative automation works for every parameter

myths.correction: Write-capable modes are ignored for writing while playback/recording is stopped.
myths.myth: Moving a fader while stopped writes automation

myths.correction: The plug-in must expose that parameter to the host.
myths.myth: A visible plug-in knob must be automatable

myths.correction: Parameter identities or slot mappings can change and create orphaned or wrong control.
myths.myth: Plug-in updates cannot affect automation mappings

myths.correction: Bypass can interrupt buffers, tails, latency, or state.
myths.myth: Automating bypass is always click-free

myths.correction: The processor may remain active and latency/state can differ.
myths.myth: Mix at zero is identical to bypass

myths.correction: Send changes effect input; return changes effect output and all sources sharing it.
myths.myth: Send and return automation sound the same

myths.correction: It stops new input; the already-generated tail can continue.
myths.myth: Lowering a send always cuts the effect tail

myths.correction: A shared return affects every source feeding that aux.
myths.myth: Lowering a return only affects one source

myths.correction: Post-fader sends follow source fader changes; pre-fader sends can remain independent.
myths.myth: Pre-fader and post-fader sends react the same to source rides

myths.correction: Compression reacts to level; phrase placement and lyrical emphasis often need human judgment.
myths.myth: Compression can replace all vocal rides

myths.correction: Intentional crescendos and accents should usually remain.
myths.myth: Volume rides should flatten every performance dynamic

myths.correction: The goal is intelligibility and musical hierarchy, not sameness.
myths.myth: Automation should make every word equally loud

myths.correction: They have different roles and routing behavior.
myths.myth: Master fader and Stereo Output are the same in Logic

myths.correction: A VCA controls assigned channel levels; an aux controls summed audio.
myths.myth: VCA and aux automation are the same

myths.correction: The placement of the bus fader and processor determines what is driven and what is only blended.
myths.myth: Bus automation never changes compressor behavior

myths.correction: Grouped faders and different starting positions can produce confusing relative behavior.
myths.myth: Group automation cannot create offsets

myths.correction: Automation often shapes section contrast, transitions, and listener attention.
myths.myth: Automation has no relationship to arrangement

myths.correction: Level rides can help, but register, arrangement, tone, and timing may be the real cause.
myths.myth: Automation fixes frequency masking

myths.correction: It may only consume headroom and trigger loudness bias.
myths.myth: Automating the chorus louder always makes it bigger

myths.correction: Some exposed parameters still reinitialize, glitch, or change latency.
myths.myth: Automating a mode or quality switch is safe if Logic exposes it

myths.correction: Plug-in render behavior, low-latency states, tails, and output automation can create discrepancies.
myths.myth: Offline bounce always matches live automation

myths.correction: Popularity is weak evidence and must be contextualized.
myths.myth: Community upvotes prove an automation technique is correct

myths.correction: The appropriate time scale, gesture, and control point depend on performance and arrangement.
myths.myth: A single automation workflow is best for every genre

myths.correction: Improvement supports a hypothesis but can be confounded by level, timing, or another simultaneous change.
myths.myth: If automation made something better, the diagnosis is proven
